description.narrative: Future Forums overall objective is to encourage intellectual research and thinking, to positively influence the policy narrative in Cambodia at a local, national and international level, employing evidence-based policy debate, analysis and recommendations in order to contribute to democratic, political and socio-economic change that will benefit all people of Cambodia. A special focus is on outreach to youth, women, grassroot communities and minorities.

Kärnstödet till Future Forum syftar till att bidra till genomförandet av ett program med titeln "Young Researchers Programme" (2020-2024). Future Forum är en kambodjansk tankesmedja som fokuserar på forskning, analys och offentlig politik. Tankesmedjan grundades 2015.
Huvudsyftet med tankesmedjan är att uppmuntra oberoende samhällsvetenskaplig forskning och tänkande och genom detta positivt påverka den kambodjanska politiska berättelsen och stimulera en evidensbaserad politisk debatt. Future Forum har också inrättats för att tillgodose behovet av fler oberoende analytiker och forskare som kan bedriva objektiv politisk forskning. Tankesmedjan strävar efter att inkludera ett stort antal aktörer i sin verksamhet och sina aktiviteter, inklusive olika politiska partier, regeringen, statsförvaltningen och det civila samhället. Ungdomar och studenter är en viktig målgrupp. En särskild ansträngning görs för att inkludera grupper som inte alltid hörs i den politiska och sociala debatten, såsom kvinnor, gräsrotsgrupper och etniska, religiösa och sociala minoriteter samt personer med funktionsnedsättning.

The core support to Future Forum aims to contribute to the implementation of a programme entitled “the Young Researchers Programme” (2020-2024). Future Forum is a Cambodian think tank that focuses on research, analysis and public policy. The think tank was established in 2015.
The main objective of the think tank is to encourage independent social scientific research and thinking and through that positively influence the Cambodian policy narrative and stimulate an evidence-based policy debate. Future Forum is also set up to respond to the need for more independent analysts and researchers that can conduct objective policy research. The think tank strives to include a wide number of actors in its operations and activities, including different political parties, the government, the state administration and civil society. Young people and students are an important target group. A special effort is made to include groups that are not always heard in policy and social debate, such as women, grassroots groups, and ethnic, religious and social minorities and persons living with disability.

Consolidation and Expansion of Research Initiatives
In 2021, Future Forum continued to expand its role as a policy research hub in Cambodia, with a particular focus on its flagship initiative, the Young Researcher Programme (YRP). Having evolved since the organisations inception in 2015, the YRP took a more formal shape in 2018 as a one-year intensive training and coaching programme for young Cambodian graduates and professionals. The programme combines structured training in policy research and analysis with practical writing exercises, peer review, and public dissemination through national and regional platforms.
The YRP saw several output from its fellows, including four policy research papers in the fields of urban studies, public health, tourism, and digital currency. These were published in the Journal of Future Cambodia in mid-2022. Additionally, ten policy-related opinion pieces and commentaries were featured in different local and international outlets, such as The Phnom Penh Post, The Diplomat, and SEA Globe.
Parallel to the YRP, Future Forum engaged in several high-profile research partnerships. These included contributions to the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) Monitor, the third volume of the Cambodia 2040 publication series with Konrad Adenauer Stiftung, and a COVID-19 Economic Impact Study in collaboration with The Asia Foundation and Angkor Research. The organisation also continued its analysis of the Cambodian microfinance sector and launched the "Research Design through a Social Inclusion Lens" project to support civic engagement. These initiatives demonstrated the organisations growing role as both a training institute and a research partner in national development discourse.
Knowledge Dissemination and Community Engagement
In 2022 FF continued to grow in both programme outputs and stakeholder engagement. Research generated by the YRP and affiliated projects began reaching broader audiences, with publications and edited volumes highlighting 28 development topics ranging from monetary policy to the fourth industrial revolution.
Future Forum also deepened its efforts to build a sustainable Community of Researchersan active network of policy-focused contributors engaged in peer learning and collaborative research. This initiative served to reinforce the organisations position as a platform for inclusive and evidence-based public discourse.
Outreach, Inclusion, and Organisational Reflection
In 2023, Future Forum received a record number of applications for the YRP201 in totaldemonstrating growing interest and visibility among the organisations target audience, particularly among women. Although six fellows dropped out during the course of the programme, the remaining cohort contributed to several new working papers and maintained focus on critical thinking, research methodology, and policy analysis.
A notable achievement in 2023 was the launch of Khmer-language podcasts, produced from fellows research outputs and distributed via Voice of America and Facebook. This initiative responded directly to previous recommendations from Sida and significantly broadened the reach of Future Forums content to non-English-speaking audiences. The organisation aims to maintain monthly podcast production going forward.
Efforts to integrate Gender Equality, Disability, and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) into programme activities were also observed. Future Forum demonstrated ambition in this area, although Sida would have liked to see even stronger ommitment and integration in programme efforts.
At the organisational level, however, certain structural gaps remained. The position of Deputy Director was unfilled, with no current plans for recruitment, raising concerns about internal capacity and leadership delegation. Additionally, the lack of a formal Chair of the Board of Directors was flagged as a governance risk. Sida emphasised the importance of this role in providing strategic oversight and holding the President accountable, including on matters such as compensation and institutional decision-making.
Despite challenges, Future Forum maintained a strong administrative reputation, demonstrating timely reporting, responsiveness, and openness in dialogue with partners
Two cases that reflect FF results
Case 1: Uptake of Policy Research on Urban Pedestrianisation by Municipal Authorities
Future Forums Young Researcher Programme (YRP) alumnus, Aronsakda, developed policy recommendations focused on the pedestrianisation of Sisowath Quay in Phnom Penh. His work centred on improving urban mobility and public space use through non-motorised transport infrastructure.
Impact and change: In 2022, Future Forum facilitated a public event in partnership with Good City Foundation to present the research findings and recommendations. Two municipal officials participated in the event, and supplementary materialspolicy commentaries, visual designs, and photo documentationwere submitted directly to City Hall. In April 2024, Phnom Penh Capital Administration announced a pedestrianisation plan covering 57 hectares of the city centre, with implementation scheduled to begin in February 2025. This policy shift aligns with the core proposals put forward by the researcher and illustrates how targeted knowledge dissemination contributed to informing municipal planning.
Case 2: Contribution to National Dialogue on Public Transport Reform
In January 2024, a young Research Fellow published a policy commentary advocating for the introduction of dedicated bus lanes and integrated infrastructure for non-motorised transport within Phnom Penhs public transport system.
Impact and change: Following the publication, the Prime Minister referenced the challenges facing public bus ridership during a public infrastructure ceremony in June 2024. The Phnom Penh Capital Administration also assessed the feasibility of dedicated bus lanes. This directive was reinforced by the head of the Municipal Public Transport Authority, who confirmed their intention to explore the integration of such lanes. The alignment of these public statements with the policy issues raised in the commentary reflects an example of how evidence-based analysis can inform and shape governmental priorities and responses.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
